chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Adib, said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Shu'ayb al-Saqqaf, known as Abu Salih, narrated to us, raising it to some of the companions of Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both).

He said: I entered upon him, and he said: 'Our Shias must not dispense with four things: a cloth upon which they pray, a ring with which they seal, a miswak with which they clean their teeth, and a tasbih (prayer beads) made from the clay of the grave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), containing thirty-three beads. Whenever they turn them while remembering Allah, forty good deeds are recorded for each bead; and if they turn them while heedless, playing with them, twenty good deeds are recorded for them.'

key_terms.خُمْرَة: A cloth or piece of fabric used as a prayer mat or covering.
key_terms.سُبْحَة: Prayer beads used for counting dhikr.
key_terms.سِوَاك: A twig used for cleaning teeth, a prophetic sunnah.
key_terms.طِينُ قَبْرِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Clay from the grave of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him).

ai.seo_question: What are the four essential items Shia Muslims are advised to keep according to Imam Musa al-Kadhim?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) instructed his followers to retain four specific items for daily religious practice: a prayer cloth, a ring, a miswak, and prayer beads made from the clay of Imam al-Baqir's grave. The hadith emphasizes the spiritual merit of using these items for dhikr, noting that even casual use yields significant rewards.
